review.justification: A complete basic arcade loop with pursuing, firing enemies, visible lives/score, controls help and restart overlay. Reverse collision loops are readable. Movement and cooldowns depend on frame rate; respawning without immunity can consume lives immediately, and the fixed canvas lacks responsive sizing.

specification.userPrompt: Create a new project for this work (e.g. `Tank Combat Arcade`) and build a top-down tank combat arcade game there. Write the entire game as a single self-contained file at `workspace/index.html` IN THAT NEW PROJECT (HTML + inline `<style>` + inline `<script>`, no external assets, no build step). The player controls a tank with arrow keys (or WASD), fires projectiles with space, and fights at least one enemy tank. Track a score on screen. Make keyboard input observable in the browser: expose `window.gameState = gameState` or update a `document.body.dataset.inputTick` value inside key handlers so automated runtime checks can see input activity. The first concrete deliverable is the index.html file inside the new project — write it now. TANK_COMBAT_HTML_SHAPE: write one complete `index.html` document in a single workspace `write_file` call. Use exactly this source shape: `<!doctype html><html><head><style>...</style></head><body>...<canvas id="game"></canvas>...<script>/* all game JavaScript here */</script></body></html>`. All JavaScript must be inside that one inline `<script>` block before `</body>`: declarations, functions, querySelector/addEventListener calls, key handlers, requestAnimationFrame game loop, projectiles, collision, score, and `window.gameState = gameState`. Do not place `const`, `let`, `var`, `function`, `querySelector`, `addEventListener`, or `requestAnimationFrame` after `</script>`, after `</body>`, or after `</html>`. If `write_file` is rejected for JavaScript outside a script tag, do not keep patching fragments; immediately re-emit the entire corrected HTML file from `<!doctype html>` through `</html>` with all JS inside the script block.
specification.scenarioBrief: Meester creates a project, recruits a developer, and ships a playable top-down tank combat arcade game in a single HTML file.

Use the `code-review` (Code Review) craftbook for this self-contained local evaluation. Open `source/craftbook-eval-brief.md` first, then follow the craftbook's actual steps and gates through its terminal step. Complete this request: Review one staged change set and deliver a gated report.

The change set is snapshotted ahead of time into the project artifacts drawer at `reviews/<reviewId>/`: `manifest.json` (kind, base/head, changed files, and — for branch reviews — the commit list) plus `changes.diff` (the unified diff). Three steps:

2. **Report** — walk the diff and write `reviews/<reviewId>/report.md` (Summary, severity-ranked Findings table with file:line citations, Verdict)
3. **Done** — stamp the verdict to task notes

specification.userPrompt: Create a new project for this work (e.g. `Tank Combat Arcade`) and build a top-down tank combat arcade game there. Write the entire game as a single self-contained file at `workspace/index.html` IN THAT NEW PROJECT (HTML + inline `<style>` + inline `<script>`, no external assets, no build step). The player controls a tank with arrow keys (or WASD), fires projectiles with space, and fights at least one enemy tank. Track a score on screen. Make keyboard input observable in the browser: expose `window.gameState = gameState` or update a `document.body.dataset.inputTick` value inside key handlers so automated runtime checks can see input activity. The first concrete deliverable is the index.html file inside the new project — write it now. TANK_COMBAT_HTML_SHAPE: write one complete `index.html` document in a single workspace `write_file` call. Use exactly this source shape: `<!doctype html><html><head><style>...</style></head><body>...<canvas id="game"></canvas>...<script>/* all game JavaScript here */</script></body></html>`. All JavaScript must be inside that one inline `<script>` block before `</body>`: declarations, functions, querySelector/addEventListener calls, key handlers, requestAnimationFrame game loop, projectiles, collision, score, and `window.gameState = gameState`. Do not place `const`, `let`, `var`, `function`, `querySelector`, `addEventListener`, or `requestAnimationFrame` after `</script>`, after `</body>`, or after `</html>`. If `write_file` is rejected for JavaScript outside a script tag, do not keep patching fragments; immediately re-emit the entire corrected HTML file from `<!doctype html>` through `</html>` with all JS inside the script block.

# Final M5 Max dual-engine scorecard — native 0.1.54

**Complete: 516/516 planned trials, three repetitions for every treatment, and zero pending artifact reviews.** Qwen3.8 27B Q4 on llama.cpp recorded the most passes (104/129) and highest mean fixed score (8.26/10). Gemma4 12B Q4 on llama.cpp had the shortest median trial duration (3.89 minutes), with 86/128 eligible passes and one preserved infrastructure exclusion. MLX used substantially less sampled process RSS for both models.

These are comparisons of the installed model/engine configurations on this device. Their quantization formats and speculative decoding differ. Passing the frozen gates does not establish polished or fully correct work: the independent artifact reviews and failure investigations below expose material gaps in some passing outputs.

Execution: **2026-10-28T00:10:08.465Z → 2026-11-02T21:37:22.911Z**, UTC. Cumulative recorded trial time: **134.97 hours** (excludes between-trial setup and recovery gaps). Final supervisor state is `trials-complete`; the driver and inference processes exited. Read-only process inspection at 22:26 UTC found no campaign runner or local inference process. No pending execution needs restarting.

Primary records: [campaign.json](<evals/runs/scorecard-2026-10-27-m5max-native-0.1.54/campaign.json>), [final-analysis.json](<evals/runs/scorecard-2026-10-27-m5max-native-0.1.54/final-analysis.json>), [judging.md](<evals/runs/scorecard-2026-10-27-m5max-native-0.1.54/judging.md>), [codex-inline-judge.json](<evals/runs/scorecard-2026-10-27-m5max-native-0.1.54/codex-inline-judge.json>), [final-failure-evidence.md](<evals/runs/scorecard-2026-10-27-m5max-native-0.1.54/final-failure-evidence.md>). The original runner's [report.md](<evals/runs/scorecard-2026-10-27-m5max-native-0.1.54/report.md>) and [trials.csv](<evals/runs/scorecard-2026-10-27-m5max-native-0.1.54/trials.csv>) remain unchanged. This report is the reconciled comparison, including telemetry caveats and advisory findings.

## Scope, counting and scoring

The 43 suite/scenario entries are core 11, productivity 13, developer 10 and complex-work 9. There are 41 distinct scenario IDs; `plan-and-estimate` and `conflict-synthesis` intentionally occur in both core and productivity. Each suite membership keeps its own three repetitions. Four targets × 43 entries × three repetitions = **516 unique planned and recorded cells**, grouped into **172 treatments**, each containing exactly repetitions 1, 2 and 3. All 516 run directories are distinct, with result, facts, fixed score, host record and postmortem. No trial was replaced or retried.

There are **349 passes, 165 model-classified failures and two infrastructure-classified exclusions**. The eligible aggregate denominator is 514. All 516 count toward execution completion and all 516 remain in performance summaries. Exclusions are displayed explicitly; their original fixed scores and failed outcomes remain in the evidence. “Model” is the frozen accounting class, not a conclusion that the underlying cause is model capability.

The fixed `eval-run-fixed-v1` composite is the saved deterministic result: completion 40%, output quality 25%, process efficiency 20% and behavior 15%. Efficiency reflects the frozen budget/tool-use rules; throughput and memory are reported separately. No score was recomputed to accommodate later findings. The artifact judge is a separate 0–10 advisory assessment and never changes a fixed score or pass.

Each treatment has only three repetitions. Counts expose repeatability within this campaign; they do not justify precise population estimates or claims of statistical significance. Overall means give equal weight to each recorded eligible trial, so suites contribute according to their scenario counts. Hardware load, caching and chronology can affect timings even with rotating target order.

## In-trial performance and coverage

Latency is measured from trial start. First-token latency includes daemon boot and queueing; it is not the first turn's engine-only TTFT. First action is the first observed tool call. First artifact is the first observed file/artifact write, which can be an intermediate file rather than the final deliverable. Missing observations remain **unknown**.

Decode rates use `metrics.derived.genTokensPerSec`, never the low-token preflight or whole-trial tokens/wall-time fallback. For llama.cpp, each trial rate is generated tokens divided by logged decode time; for MLX, each trial rate is the median of active-decode heartbeat rates. Tables take medians across trials, so these are different measurement estimators. MLX logs prefill token counts without durations: **all MLX prefill rates are unknown**. Engine-log token totals describe observed inference work and can include repeated/cache-related work; they are not unique user text or provider billing.

RSS is the sampled process-tree total (daemon plus descendants), reported in the collector's MB convention. Tables show the median of trial peaks and, separately, the largest observed peak. Shared mappings can affect RSS accounting. System RAM includes the entire host and other applications. These quantities are not interchangeable with model weights or GPU allocation. **macOS GPU utilization and dedicated GPU memory are unknown**, not zero; any zero GPU placeholders in raw reports must not be read as measurements.

## Advisory artifact quality

All **228 applicable trial slots** are reconciled: **215 numeric reviews**, **12 judgeSpecMismatch** (every A/B readout) and **one noArtifact** (Gemma llama.cpp code-review repetition 3). The remaining **288 trials are notApplicable** and remain ungraded. Numeric reviews include **80 trials that failed their deterministic gate**. No external judge or subagent was invoked.

Reviews used each packet's exact scenario prompt and axis descriptions, integer 0–10 scores, the frozen rubric (5 for merely delivering the brief; 9–10 reserved for polished work), a specific justification of at most 400 characters and a review timestamp. The anchors use the default HTML axes. These are source-based reviews of the first **20 KiB** of the declared artifact, not a claim of full visual or end-to-end testing. Two petshop packets were capped: Qwen llama.cpp repetition 2 and Qwen MLX repetition 3. All packet bytes were reconciled against their source artifact; review hashes are saved in final-analysis.json.

A/B readout declares mock-service safety/mapping/signals/containment axes that do not describe its statistical report. Each mismatch has an explicit saved justification; no substitute numerical grade was invented. Four early find-vs-create packets remain preserved without scores after its scope was correctly recognized as non-judgeable.

The table below averages the declared axes within a scenario, then across the target's reviewed repetitions. These scenario rubrics measure different things, so there is deliberately **no pooled overall advisory rank**. Every entry has n=3 except Gemma llama.cpp code-review (n=2); the absent third report has no grade. The largest gaps between fixed acceptance and advisory quality are practical: tankcombat passes all 12 gates while several saved games have broken firing, scoring or collision-reset behavior; week-plan passes 5/12 despite poor grounding; invoices can look finished while bookkeeping or payee details are wrong. Meeting follow-up and document deliverables generally have stronger reviewed content. A strong score on a theme blocker report still does not mean the requested theme conversion happened.

## Concrete failure diagnoses and implications

The frozen failure modes are 153 `model-stuck`, nine `chat-stalled`, four `timeout` and one `success-check-false`. These labels explain termination, not all causes. The detailed evidence register contains every failed trial and the 23 previously reported incidents. The following clusters distinguish observations from proposed future work; no fix was applied to this campaign.

**Tool access and repair authority.** Theme round-trip fails 12/12 with required DocBlocks tools unavailable. Qwen MLX research encountered registered Wikipedia tools removed by immediate-write/file-repair restrictions. Gemma MLX tic-tac-toe repetition 3 had a real `NodeList.some` defect; isolated candidate replays passed behavior probes, but the overwrite guard rejected the shorter repair and the recovery surface omitted the patch tool its feedback requested. These are tool/repair integration findings, not reasons to increase model size. See [final-failure-evidence.md](<evals/runs/scorecard-2026-10-27-m5max-native-0.1.54/final-failure-evidence.md>) and the affected trial postmortems.

**Completion and verdict gates can accept incomplete work.** Author-linear repetition 2 accepted a manually completed task before any gated step ran; a later report remained below the unused recipe gate's size floor. API-contract-review accepted `UNMET` because the gate recognized only literal `FAIL`. Invoice verdict normalization collapsed line boundaries and hid an otherwise matching FAIL. Fanout repetition 1 selected an earlier completed root despite four children under a later invocation; only one child completed, so the result still cannot be counted as successful. These findings call for execution receipts, structured criterion results and explicit invocation identity. Evidence: [invoice-verdict-normalization-r3-replay.json](<evals/runs/scorecard-2026-10-27-m5max-native-0.1.54/invoice-verdict-normalization-r3-replay.json>) and the incident register.

**Grounding and cross-file consistency.** Week-plan's gate could accept calendar retrieval that happened after the final report, leaving the plan ungrounded. A passed invoice run left the ledger and billable entries unchanged; other invoices invented fees, addresses or the wrong payee. A/B repetition 2 repaired stats after writing its readout, producing an internally stale report; repetition 3 passed with p=0.000513 rather than the independently checked pooled-test p=0.007785. The frozen A/B gate checks the significance flag but not the p-value or confidence interval. The same task also contains an exact-schema/required-interval conflict and an unsuitable advisory rubric. These are report dependency and contract defects; the 8/12 fixed passes are preserved, not endorsed as fully correct statistics.

**Authoring must validate executable contracts.** Two author-params trials left `workPath` undefined and stopped the campaign; their infrastructure exclusions are preserved below. Qwen MLX author-linear repetition 3 saved the invalid JavaScript pattern `(?i)\bPASS\b`; repeatedly editing a correct report cannot fix a gate that does not compile. Qwen llama.cpp gate-script repetition 3 supplied a checks array to `gateResult(boolean, detail)`; controlled calls to the frozen SDK show a failed-check array is truthy and approves. That generated gate never ran in the trial, so this is a latent contract defect, not an observed erroneous approval. Evidence: [author-linear-invalid-gate-pattern-r3-replay.json](<evals/runs/scorecard-2026-10-27-m5max-native-0.1.54/author-linear-invalid-gate-pattern-r3-replay.json>), [gate-result-array-contract-r3-replay.json](<evals/runs/scorecard-2026-10-27-m5max-native-0.1.54/gate-result-array-contract-r3-replay.json>).

**Timeouts and feedback must account for active work.** Qwen llama.cpp gate-script repetition 1 waited 1,030 seconds for inference admission and had a 126,038-token prefill take 571 seconds; the watchdog ended it while inference was active. Qwen MLX petshop repetition 3 invoked genuine image generation, but the HTML repair limit terminated the trial while SDXL sampling was still active; decode continued during shutdown and no PNG was captured. These observations do not license unbounded waiting. A future bounded policy should distinguish queued, prefill, decoding and pending-tool work from repeated ineffective repairs. See [r1-qwen-llamacpp-complex-work-craftbook-author-gate-script](<evals/runs/scorecard-2026-10-27-m5max-native-0.1.54/r1-qwen-llamacpp-complex-work-craftbook-author-gate-script/craftbook-author-gate-script/craftbook-author-gate-script-qwen3-8-27b-q4-2026-10-29T16-44-56-719Z-bi1u/postmortem.md>) and [r3-qwen-mlx-core-petshop](<evals/runs/scorecard-2026-10-27-m5max-native-0.1.54/r3-qwen-mlx-core-petshop/petshop/petshop-mlx-qwen3-8-27b-q4-2026-10-31T23-20-23-986Z-iqxn/postmortem.md>).

**Artifact/type and note contracts need consistent enforcement.** Gemma MLX PowerPoint repetition 3 copied a 335-byte JSON artifact to a `.pptx` destination after failing to save a real converted deck; the gate correctly rejected it, while the copy API allowed the misleading type. Gemma llama.cpp code-review repetition 3 supplied both short `note` and detailed `content` aliases; `text ?? note ?? content` kept the short text, causing six missing-Scope rejections and no report. Canonical arguments and the same binary checks across write and copy paths would address reusable interface failure modes.

**Fanout delivery is distinct from reusable workflow execution.** The last Qwen llama.cpp run created a linear recipe with no spawn step and no children; its report gate anchored `^` without multiline matching, rejecting an otherwise present list. The last Gemma MLX run wrote direct reports and a workspace JSON recipe that was never registered. The last Gemma llama.cpp run had five rejected template writes and completed only the read step of an ad hoc task. Each had all four store reports, yet the requested reusable fanout was absent. Their recorded scores are 5.1, 5.4 and 5.4, respectively. See [r3-qwen-llamacpp-complex-work-craftbook-author-fanout](<evals/runs/scorecard-2026-10-27-m5max-native-0.1.54/r3-qwen-llamacpp-complex-work-craftbook-author-fanout/craftbook-author-fanout/craftbook-author-fanout-qwen3-8-27b-q4-2026-11-02T20-03-31-159Z-a48x/postmortem.md>), [r3-gemma-mlx-complex-work-craftbook-author-fanout](<evals/runs/scorecard-2026-10-27-m5max-native-0.1.54/r3-gemma-mlx-complex-work-craftbook-author-fanout/craftbook-author-fanout/craftbook-author-fanout-mlx-gemma4-12b-q4-2026-11-02T21-03-44-160Z-lsom/postmortem.md>) and [r3-gemma-llamacpp-complex-work-craftbook-author-fanout](<evals/runs/scorecard-2026-10-27-m5max-native-0.1.54/r3-gemma-llamacpp-complex-work-craftbook-author-fanout/craftbook-author-fanout/craftbook-author-fanout-gemma4-12b-q4-2026-11-02T21-19-48-250Z-3yci/postmortem.md>). The full repeated matrix below prevents a single late failure from being mistaken for the whole campaign.

# Supervision evidence

## 2026-10-28 01:44 UTC — first hourly review

The supervisor advanced from 10 to 12 recorded trials during this check and started the next schema-migration treatment. It remains healthy. No restart, rerun, source/build/catalog change, gate adjustment, reclassification or stop-clear was needed. All 24 native fingerprints still match native-provenance.json. All six recorded llama.cpp hosts report build 11669, revision 620d2225cc436ab0b001e3200e590e3b286ef9ab, Metal. MLX host build fields are null; MLX package provenance comes from the frozen environment record, not a fabricated native build number.

### Failed pet-shop artifacts

Both MLX pet-shop trials produced judgeable HTML but no usable raster logo. Their fixed recorded classification remains model/model-default; the following diagnoses are advisory and do not change that classification.

- **Gemma MLX:** facts.json records 32 tool calls, no generate_image, missing image-generator role, and an unchanged 3/5 gate through four delivered repair attempts. The image specialist's saved session (geza--f5b17da4-4130-4a94-a320-dc84960ce553.json) explicitly requests a PNG via generate_image and forbids write_file. Yet daemon.log:195 shows immediate-write mode restricting its surface to write_file only, followed by an index.html write at line 215. This is concrete evidence that the immediate-write framework path misroutes a binary-artifact request. Later attempts repeat shortened HTML writes rejected by the source guard (lines 979–1042). Investigate immediate-write selection and role tool filtering after the frozen campaign; do not tune this campaign or infer a model ceiling.
- **Qwen MLX:** facts.json records 26 tool calls, no generate_image and a missing image-generator role. The model invoked run_installed_script for project/generate_image (daemon.log:485–490), then narrated that its router only had delegate/consult image tools and salvaged ensure_gezel plus delegate_developer (639–641). The HTML reference existed, but no raster file appeared before the 18-minute stalled-artifact stop. Diagnose image-tool selection, specialist routing and handoff behavior. No native image-engine crash is demonstrated: the required image operation was never invoked.
- **Same-build comparison:** both llama.cpp pet-shop trials invoked generate_image once and passed. Gemma llama.cpp still has a missingExpectedRoles image-generator penalty despite successful image generation through delegate_image_generator; this indicates a role-label heuristic may undercount capability. Preserve that fixed score (7.0); inspect the heuristic separately after the campaign.

### Performance interpretation

All first 12 trials contain duration, first-token/tool/artifact latencies, in-trial decode rates, engine-log token totals, peak process-tree RSS and sampled system memory. Prefill rates are available on six llama.cpp trials; MLX prefill duration is absent and remains unknown. GPU utilization is unavailable (0/12), not zero utilization. Peak RSS sums the daemon and child processes and may include image generation. System memory includes other device activity.

The frozen collector computes llama.cpp decode as total generated tokens divided by decode seconds. MLX decode is the median active-stream pulse rate, and its output-token total is reconstructed heuristically from cumulative pulse counters (evals/src/perf-collector.ts:1011). These are different estimators; retain the distinction in the final comparison. MLX token totals may be incomplete or ambiguous around concurrent internal sessions/turn boundaries; the provider HTTP billing summary also undercounts tool/reasoning tokens, so do not substitute it or call the reconstructed total exact. Low-token preflight rates are excluded from the performance comparison.

Judging is source-based at the frozen 20 KiB cap; it does not assert rendered image quality. The HTML anchors passed minimal deterministic behavior checks, but qualitative review can still identify absent gameplay threats or misleading form submission. Those judgments stay separate from fixed composites.

## 2026-10-28 02:44 UTC — second hourly review
